findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller's set_locale
findings.body: `translate` still calls `load_locale` only for `config.locale` (line 68). The new `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` runs only in `ApplicationController#set_locale` (application_controller.rb:159). Sidekiq jobs, mailers and the console that set `I18n.locale` themselves will fall back to `:en` or the site default, but those locales may not be loaded. Lookups would then return "translation missing" instead of the fallback text. Fallbacks are also now on in every environment, because the initializer is unconditional, whereas before they were enabled only in production and profile. Consider loading the fallback locales inside `translate`, or wherever the locale is switched for jobs and mailers. The LRU cache key (line 72) also ignores the fallback chain, so a change to `default_locale` can leave stale cached strings.

contracts.action: Fallback locales are loaded on each request via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!
contracts.before_after: Before, only the request locale was loaded, and Rails fallbacks were enabled only in production and profile. After, the request locale, the site default locale and :en are all loaded, and fallbacks are on in every environment.
contracts.visible_effect: Keys missing in the user's locale show the site-default or English text instead of "translation missing".
contracts.failure_mode: Code paths that do not go through set_locale (jobs, mailers) do not load the fallback locales, so fallback lookups can miss. A failure inside load_locale would raise from set_locale and fail the request.

summary: The change is mostly sound. One concern: fallback locales are loaded only in the controller's `set_locale`, so jobs, mailers and the console can miss fallback translations. I did not check whether anything else sets the locale in those paths.
